source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability with SAEs: Probing Religion, Violence, and Geography in Large Language Models

record.tranche_reason: Applies pretrained SAE features to a new domain—religious concepts in LLMs—and reports measurements of their overlap and semantic activation contexts. This bears on indirect LLM evidence for SAE-recoverable features, but is not a direct test of superposition.
record.gate_note: The study uses Neuronpedia SAEs to measure religious-feature overlap and semantic activation texts. It states that the underlying SAEs were not revalidated. Table 1 lists several SAE configurations, but does not map each configuration to the model-level results in Tables 2 and 3. The study's findings on religion and violence are not evidence about superposition geometry or capacity competition.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained Neuronpedia SAEs as an off-the-shelf tool to audit religion–violence and religion–geography associations in five LLMs. The authors say they do not revalidate the SAEs. No result measures whether features are spread across neurons, whether SAEs recover sparse features, or anything about superposition geometry, capacity, or feature dimensionality. Its outputs are bias measures (feature-overlap counts, a Violence Association Index, crime-keyword rates in activation texts). These bear on stereotypes, not on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct; it needs the main findings added. The authors conclude that all five religions show similar intra-group cohesion. Islam has the highest Violence Association Index in all five models. Islam usually has the highest crime-keyword rate, but Hinduism exceeds it in GPT2-small and Llama3.1-8B. Geographic associations partly reflect real demographics but skew toward Europe and North America. Associations vary by model. The authors frame SAE-based structural analysis as a methodological contribution for auditing internal representations.
record.recipe_differences: The original source studies feature superposition in toy networks; this paper uses pretrained SAEs through Neuronpedia to analyze semantic overlap and activation contexts in LLMs, without testing superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported religion–violence and crime-keyword patterns vary across model groups; the paper associates this variation with architecture and training-data composition. SAE configuration-to-result mapping is not stated.
record.peer_reviewed: AEQUITAS 2025 Workshop on Fairness and Bias in AI, co-located with ECAI; accepted for presentation
record.problems: The authors do not revalidate the pretrained SAEs. The results rely on top activating features and keyword searches of activation texts; no uncertainty estimates or controls are reported. Table 1 lists multiple SAE configurations but the result tables do not identify which configuration produced each model-level result. The claimed semantic meaning of SAE features is therefore indirect.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the 20 per-religion intra-group overlap values other than Islam from Table 2's upper section to stay within the 60-row limit; these were described as broadly similar across religions. The included all-religions totals and Islam overlap values preserve the reported range and an individual category. No other reported Table 2 or Table 3 results were omitted.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, or geometry.
No analysis of the causes of polysemantic neurons.
Uses SAE features but does not measure neuron-level distribution or SAE recovery or quality. It assumes SAE features are meaningful.
No completeness, stability, or canonicity tests.

record.verdict_notes: This is a bias-audit workshop paper (AEQUITAS 2025) that treats SAE features as given. The reader's V4 'supports' label is unwarranted: interpretable-looking activation texts were assumed, not tested against any criterion bearing on superposition. Table 1 lists several SAEs per model (e.g., Gemma-2-2B att-16k, res-16k, res-65k) without mapping them to the result columns. No controls or uncertainty are reported.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network feature/dimension sweep, sparsity-dependent transition, or geometry test.
No test of capacity competition, dedicated dimensions, or polysemanticity caused by limited capacity.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.

Provides indirect evidence from pretrained SAE features and their activation contexts, but does not establish that the features are complete, faithful, or causally used by the LLM; does not measure features spread across neurons.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical, or the model's true representational units.
Does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.
